title: Story Writing — complete arc from a given outline
notes: **What it is:** a COMPLETE narrative arc judged on plot — situation → problem → turning point → resolution → (often) a quiet moral.

**Structure:** Opening (if the prompt gives a first line, USE it verbatim and continue) → Complication → Rising action → Climax (the decisive moment — slow down here) → Resolution + realisation/moral.

**Tense machinery:** past simple drives the plot; past continuous paints background ('I was dawdling home'); past perfect marks earlier events ('which she had lost'); direct speech at the climax adds life.
**Keep ONE tense zone and ONE narrator** — drifting between present and past, or I/he, breaks the story.
**Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).
examShortTricks: Trick 1: Story skeleton: setting → conflict → rising action → climax → resolution; plan the CLIMAX first, then work backwards — plots fail without a designed turning point.
Trick 2: Show, don't tell: replace 'he was scared' with 'his hands shook as he reached the door' — one shown detail per paragraph lifts the band.
Trick 3: Dialogue rule: every line of dialogue must reveal character or advance plot; two lines are better than five flat ones.
Trick 4: Title and moral: end with a line that echoes the title — circular closure earns the structure mark.
practiceQuestions: Q. Develop a story beginning: 'It was raining heavily that night...' (5 marks) — set scene, introduce conflict, climax, resolution with a title.
Q. What makes a story's climax effective? (1 mark) — it resolves the central conflict at maximum tension.
